title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads Agentic Inference Performance on MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Provisional (not yet MLCommons-verified) MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 results show NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 delivering 5x-10x throughput per provisioned kilowatt and 3x-5x end-to-end interactivity versus verified GB300 NVL72 on agentic workloads (Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). NVIDIA attributes the gains to HBM4, Tensor Cores and sixth-generation NVLink plus context-aware serving (prefix caching, Dynamo routing, disaggregated prefill/decode) and model-specific kernels.

insights.claim: Provisional MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 results show NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 delivering over 10x the throughput per kilowatt of provisioned power of GB300 NVL72 on Kimi K3 at a shared minimum end-to-end interactivity of 50 tokens per second per user.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: In power-constrained data centers, tokens per kW is the revenue metric — a 10x step implies Rubin sharply lowers inference cost per token and pressures prior-gen rental pricing.
insights.locator: In MLPerf Endpoints v1.0, provisional NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 results

insights.claim: Across models, Vera Rubin NVL72 versus GB300 NVL72 showed throughput-per-provisioned-kW ratios of 10x on Kimi K3, 9x on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and 5x on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and E2E interactivity ratios of 3x, 5x and 3x respectively at matched concurrency.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: Gains are largest on the biggest model and smallest on the small 35B-A3B MoE, so Rubin's edge is most valuable for frontier-scale agent serving.
insights.locator: Table 1. Throughput per kilowatt and E2E interactivity ratios

insights.claim: The headline Kimi K3 comparison pits a 32-accelerator Vera Rubin NVL72 run (1,024 concurrent queries, 41,414.2 tokens/sec, 100.89 kW) against a 48-accelerator GB300 NVL72 run (48 queries, 2,210.4 tokens/sec, 60 kW); at matched 1,024-query concurrency GB300 reached only 16.8 tokens/sec per user versus 50.4 for Vera Rubin.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: The 10x is measured on provisioned power at a chosen interactivity floor with very different operating points — treat it as a best-case framing and await MLCommons verification.

insights.claim: The Vera Rubin NVL72 Endpoints results are provisional and pending MLCommons verification and peer review, while the GB300 NVL72 results they are compared against are verified.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: Headline multiples could change after review; watch the verified results on endpoints.mlcommons.org.
insights.quote: Pending MLCommons Association verification, results are subject to change pending peer review.

insights.claim: Higher throughput per kilowatt lets operators run more AI agents simultaneously within the same power budget while meeting the same responsiveness requirement.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: With power as the binding constraint on AI capacity, perf-per-watt upgrades translate directly into revenue capacity per site — a driver for Rubin replacement demand.
insights.quote: Higher throughput per kilowatt enables organizations to run more agents simultaneously within the same power budget while meeting the same responsiveness requirement.
insights.locator: Higher throughput per kilowatt enables organizations

insights.claim: Agentic workloads stress inference systems differently: coding trajectories accumulate conversation history over many turns and enterprise workflows reuse shared instructions, tool definitions and business rules, so context length grows across a session.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: Growing context per session raises memory (HBM, KV cache) intensity of inference — supportive of HBM4 and memory-tier demand.
insights.locator: The serving demands of multi-turn agentic AI

insights.claim: MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 benchmarks serving capacity versus responsiveness through API endpoints on coding and enterprise workflows, checking generated tool calls against reference values and running separate SWE-bench Verified evaluations to confirm faster serving preserves model quality.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: A new endpoint-level agentic benchmark gives investors a standardized way to compare inference vendors on throughput per kW vs latency.
insights.locator: MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 evaluates this balance

insights.claim: NVIDIA Rubin GPUs combine HBM4 memory for fast access to weights and conversation state, Tensor Cores for matrix math, and sixth-generation NVLink for cross-GPU communication to meet agentic inference demands.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: HBM4 is central to Rubin's inference story — read-through to HBM4 suppliers' volume ramp.
insights.locator: Hardware and software optimizations for agentic inference

insights.claim: Context-aware serving — prefix caching, state reuse, NVIDIA Dynamo routing and disaggregated prefill/decode serving — reduces redundant computation and balances load for agentic inference, e.g. Kimi pairs disaggregated serving with prefill changes that cut GPU synchronization waits.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: Much of the inference gain is software (Dynamo), deepening NVIDIA's full-stack moat beyond silicon.

insights.claim: Model-specific GPU execution adds further gains: DeepSeek's MegaMoE kernel exploits Rubin GPU locality and matrix-multiply instructions, and Qwen's multi-token prediction pairs token proposals with Tensor Core verification to reduce sequential decoding steps.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weight model developers are optimizing kernels for NVIDIA Rubin, reinforcing CUDA as the default target for leading models.
insights.locator: Table 2. Software optimizations improve context reuse

insights.claim: NVIDIA argues agentic inference performance depends on co-design across hardware, system architecture and serving software rather than raw chip specs alone.
insights.speaker: Zhihan Jiang
insights.so_what: Framing favors integrated full-stack vendors over merchant-chip or ASIC competitors that lack a mature serving stack.
insights.quote: Agentic inference performance depends on co-design across hardware, system architecture, and serving software.
insights.locator: More productive infrastructure for agentic AI
